title: I Remade Shining Force 1 , my favourite childhood RPG. With AI.
author: Exped1ter001
selftext:
Hello Everyone! 

I recently had some free time and was looking at all the available tool to help aid people without art skills or programming experience. 

I know some hardcore fans of shining force might not like a game made with AI tools but there might be some who will appreciate what I have built. 

Although I used ai tools this took an extreme amount of effort and dedication for 30 days, but I have always wanted to remake this game so I pushed through. 

Here is my video going over the basics of what I have built. ( I don’t make videos often so it’s not that great) 

https://youtu.be/NuYOANgSh9w

I have an hour long play though video but I deleted it because I don’t think many people would want to watch me playing shining force for an hour. 

Let me know what you think ! 

I have a completely playable with save slots game from the intro to Alterone. If I push hard I should be able to finish chapter one. I have added abilities and skill trees for all the characters. In the video they are just place holders. I have a new promotion system. Many things added and yet so much is just like it was 30 years ago.

One thing I have NOT implemented yet is the cutscene battles. Currently it’s real time combat. I am working on cutscene but I am actually having fun playing the realtime with shining force I might add an option to play either or.

comments.author: TopTippityTop
comments.body: Ooooh I used to LOVE shining force as well! Cool!

replies.author: Exped1ter001
replies.body:
Thanks a lot ! , yes my battle system is turn based. I called it real time just to differentiate from the cutscene style. 

Honestly the turn based non cut scene has its advantages!  It makes for abilities to really be visible and actually speeds up the battles enough to add more enemies. I’m honestly impressed with how far I got with no game dev training. ( art or programming).  I’ll look into Lora. I am brand new to this and only used grok , photoshop for visuals. 

When I am done chapter one I’ll see if anyone interested wants to play it. My brother loves playing what I built so far.

replies.author: TopTippityTop
replies.body:
I think I prefer without the cutscenes as well. To do what I suggested, for both getting consistency, faster outputs, and better style, do the following:

- Install comfyui. There are easy install versions out there if you want (I use 'Stability Matrix'). You'll probably need to have 6gb of vram at least, or some ram (slow) to compensate. The more vram the faster your outputs will be... Though with small posted it may not be that significant a difference. Comfy looks threatening at first, but all you have to do is get workflows and learn the basics.

- Go to civitai.com and look for basic models and Loras for it. I suggest you focus on this: Flux Klein 9b. It has editing capabilities and pretty decent generation quality/time. Get that base models, then look for Loras. A Lora is a smaller model which modifies the larger "checkpoint" model. You probably want these types of Loras: 

1 for style (pixel art, or whatever you want to go for), 

1 for theme (fantasy. May not be needed, as it's a pretty common theme in the training data),

1 for multiview, ir top-down pov,

1 for the animation, of you find any. Klein has edit capabilities, so it'll be able to give you different poses if you can describe them, but it's always helpful if you can find a model that gets you there more consistently.

- Once you've gotten the software and basic models installed in their proper folders, go back to civitai and look for workflows for Klein 9b. A workflow is a sequence of nodes which connected helps you generate an image in a way you want. You'll need a good text to image (t2i), one good image to image (i2i) for editing, one with multireferences, in case you want to reference specific things for your designs. You may not need it. There are also workflows which focus on animating characters.

- Then go to comfy, load one of the workflows, plug your models in the nodes, type your prompt and... Magic. I know there's some extra overhead, but with a bit of practice and getting used to, you can batch create your assets with higher quality and consistency.

Good luck

comments.author: Bodybag28
comments.body: I've been creating my own game similar to Shining Force for a couple years and currently have been using AI art for most tilesets and portraits.  I subscribed to your channel.  If you ever need someone to play test or bounce ideas off of, let me know.

replies.author: Exped1ter001
replies.body:
That’s great ! I loved SF , it was the first game I pulled all nighters playing.  I have some fights burnt into my memory. 

I plan to let people play what I built when I finish chapter one.  Right now it’s fully playable, you can egress from fights and level your characters up as much as the starting fights will allow. You can save etc. but I would like to release a polished chapter one

Thanks , I might make my own SRPG after this but I just had the urge to remake SF1 and when I’m motivated with something I can’t really stop.

comments.author: Douglas12dsd
comments.body:
Amazing work. Although I'm not very fond of SRPGs, especially older ones due to their slower speed, I can see myself playing the heck of it, specially if it's easy to mod. 


When making a game, you are also unknownlingy developing an engine as well, so even if you can't publish the game due to copyright reasons, you can remove everything Shining Force related from it and use it as an engine for your future SRPG games.

replies.author: Exped1ter001
replies.body: That’s a good point. All the tools I made etc could easily swap out everything and be a completely different game. This version is a bit faster because I took out the cutscene battles. I’ll make another video showing an actual play through.
